## NLTK dot2img runs Graphviz 'dot' without the trusted-exec chokepoint, enabling local code execution via a writable PATH element

Source-reported by [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7mxv-7h3q-9324).

CVE-2026-128134 (official CVSS 7.8): Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img resolves the Graphviz dot executable through PATH but invokes the resulting absolute executable without routing through spawn_trusted, so resolve_trusted_executable ownership and writability validation and safe_env loader environment scrubbing do not run. A local low-privileged attacker who can write to a directory on a POSIX victim's PATH can plant or replace dot, and code executes as the victim when dot2img is called directly or DependencyGraph.repr_svg renders a graph.

**What to do:** Upgrade to a fixed release: nltk 3.10.4.

**Limitations:** Source-reported; SecOpsAI did not reproduce the issue.

## Collection scope

SecOpsAI watched 28 sources for this edition; all were current. 5 package registries are watched through release metadata only, without scanning package contents. This is not complete coverage of every source or registry.
